eta_trace.note: Per-sample ETA record for analysis, not display. 'our_eta_seconds' is Platterpus's smoothed album estimate; 'actual_remaining_seconds' is what really remained (finish − 'at') so estimate-vs-actual is directly visible; 'cyanrip_eta' is cyanrip's own per-op estimate (untrusted); 'read_speed' is the -S value in effect (0 = drive max); 'track'/'activity' are the event context for a jump; 'at' is the PC wall-clock time. 'state' names the branch that produced the sample — computed (a fresh rate measurement), held_no_rate / held_over_ceiling (the previous estimate re-shown), rereading (a secure re-read has the album bar pinned) or stalled (neither liveness signal moved) — so a held value is never mistaken for a measurement; 'reread_pass' counts restarts of the current track's read (0 = first read). Compare against 'timing'.

url="$2"
branch="$3"
pin="$4"

# $1 is a path RELATIVE TO $HOME, and $HOME is expanded HERE — at the point of
# use, inside the container's own shell. Passing a pre-baked "$HOME/..." string
# does NOT work: parameter expansion does not recurse, so it stayed literal and
# every path became a relative one under a directory named '$HOME'. See
# FORK_SOURCE_SUBPATH for the full post-mortem.
src="$HOME/$1"
url="$2"
branch="$3"
pin="$4"
# $6 — `meson setup` options for THIS pin, or empty. Word-split deliberately
# (the one place in this script that wants splitting), because it is either
# empty or a short list of `-Dkey=value`. Every element was validated against an
# allowlist in Python before it got here: see `_clean_build_options` in
# ripper_manifest.py for why the manifest's build command is PARSED and never
# executed. Empty is the correct value for every commit predating the option —
# round 11 §0 measured that meson fails the WHOLE configure on an unknown -D, so
# a constant flag here would break the downgrade path to our own current pin.
meson_opts="${6-}"
# $7 — the FULL 40-character commit HEAD must be, or empty when this Platterpus
# never recorded one for $4 (a newer manifest release, a commit an operator
# typed). See `full_commit_for` in fork_source.py for why the pin itself stays
# short.
full="${7-}"

# These four lines are the ones that would have ended the v0.6.4b2 hunt in
# seconds. The failure was entirely visible in a path and nobody printed it.
echo "platterpus: HOME=$HOME"
echo "platterpus: cwd=$(pwd)"
echo "platterpus: source tree=$src"
echo "platterpus: requested pin=$pin branch=$branch"
case "$src" in
  /*) : ;;
  *) echo "platterpus: FATAL source tree is not an absolute path: $src" >&2
     exit 1 ;;
esac
case "$src" in
  *'$'*) echo "platterpus: FATAL source tree contains an unexpanded variable:" \
              "$src — this is the v0.6.4b2 defect" >&2
         exit 1 ;;
esac

if [ -d "$src/.git" ]; then
  echo "platterpus: reusing existing clone, fetching $branch"
  git -C "$src" remote set-url origin "$url"
  git -C "$src" fetch --force origin "$branch"
else
  echo "platterpus: no clone at $src — cloning $branch"
  git clone --branch "$branch" "$url" "$src"
fi
# Detach onto the verified commit — the FULL one when we have it, because a short
# name is resolved as a ref before it is resolved as a commit, so a tag or branch
# spelled like the pin would win. `--force` discards a half-finished previous
# attempt; the tree is a build cache we own, never the user's work.
git -C "$src" checkout --force --detach "${full:-$pin}"

# fork's meson `vcs_tag` prints `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, and git sizes a
# short hash by how many objects the repository holds: seven characters until
# a clone passes about 16,000 objects, eight after. The fork's repository passed
# that line with `.29`, so a reused clone built a tag ending `-g8d2ca726` where
# the published build, and the pin, end `-g8d2ca72`, and the check
# below refused a correct build (the owner's install of 0.7.120, 2026-11-04).

echo "platterpus: HEAD short=$(git -C "$src" rev-parse --short HEAD)"

# short.

# the whole point: the steps that follow are `sudo install` over

# and export are exactly where a correct build could still go astray.

         "in place" >&2

# use, inside the container's own shell. Passing a pre-baked "$HOME/..." string
# does NOT work: parameter expansion does not recurse, so it stayed literal and
# every path became a relative one under a directory named '$HOME'. See
# FORK_SOURCE_SUBPATH for the full post-mortem.
src="$HOME/$1"
url="$2"
branch="$3"
pin="$4"
# $6 — `meson setup` options for THIS pin, or empty. Word-split deliberately
# (the one place in this script that wants splitting), because it is either

# ripper_manifest.py for why the manifest's build command is PARSED and never
# executed. Empty is the correct value for every commit predating the option —
# round 11 §0 measured that meson fails the WHOLE configure on an unknown -D, so
# a constant flag here would break the downgrade path to our own current pin.
meson_opts="${6-}"
# $7 — the FULL 40-character commit HEAD must be, or empty when this Platterpus
# never recorded one for $4 (a newer manifest release, a commit an operator
# typed). See `full_commit_for` in fork_source.py for why the pin itself stays
# short.
full="${7-}"

# seconds. The failure was entirely visible in a path and nobody printed it.
echo "platterpus: HOME=$HOME"
echo "platterpus: cwd=$(pwd)"
echo "platterpus: source tree=$src"
echo "platterpus: requested pin=$pin branch=$branch"
case "$src" in
  /*) : ;;
  *) echo "platterpus: FATAL source tree is not an absolute path: $src" >&2
     exit 1 ;;
esac
case "$src" in
  *'$'*) echo "platterpus: FATAL source tree contains an unexpanded variable:" \
              "$src — this is the v0.6.4b2 defect" >&2
         exit 1 ;;
esac

  echo "platterpus: reusing existing clone, fetching $branch"
  git -C "$src" remote set-url origin "$url"
  git -C "$src" fetch --force origin "$branch"
else

  git clone --branch "$branch" "$url" "$src"
fi

# name is resolved as a ref before it is resolved as a commit, so a tag or branch

# attempt; the tree is a build cache we own, never the user's work.

# a clone passes about 16,000 objects, eight after. The fork's repository passed

  meson setup $meson_opts "$src/build" "$src"

# The build step's own self-check. Previously the first time anyone learned the
# banner was wrong was three commands later, in the verify step, which reported

# that produced it.

# problem accurately and still leaves the wrong ripper on the ripping path,

    case "$_banner" in
      *"($5"[0-9a-f]*)

             "than the published tag; the source tree's git abbreviates it" \
             "differently, so the binary's tag would not match the pin" >&2 ;;

# use, inside the container's own shell. Passing a pre-baked "$HOME/..." string
# does NOT work: parameter expansion does not recurse, so it stayed literal and
# every path became a relative one under a directory named '$HOME'. See
# FORK_SOURCE_SUBPATH for the full post-mortem.
src="$HOME/$1"
url="$2"
branch="$3"
pin="$4"
# $6 — `meson setup` options for THIS pin, or empty. Word-split deliberately
# (the one place in this script that wants splitting), because it is either
# empty or a short list of `-Dkey=value`. Every element was validated against an
# allowlist in Python before it got here: see `_clean_build_options` in
# ripper_manifest.py for why the manifest's build command is PARSED and never
# executed. Empty is the correct value for every commit predating the option —
# round 11 §0 measured that meson fails the WHOLE configure on an unknown -D, so
# a constant flag here would break the downgrade path to our own current pin.
meson_opts="${6-}"
# $7 — the FULL 40-character commit HEAD must be, or empty when this Platterpus
# never recorded one for $4 (a newer manifest release, a commit an operator
# typed). See `full_commit_for` in fork_source.py for why the pin itself stays
# short.
full="${7-}"

# These four lines are the ones that would have ended the v0.6.4b2 hunt in
# seconds. The failure was entirely visible in a path and nobody printed it.
echo "platterpus: HOME=$HOME"
echo "platterpus: cwd=$(pwd)"
echo "platterpus: source tree=$src"
echo "platterpus: requested pin=$pin branch=$branch"
case "$src" in
  /*) : ;;
  *) echo "platterpus: FATAL source tree is not an absolute path: $src" >&2
     exit 1 ;;
esac
case "$src" in
  *'$'*) echo "platterpus: FATAL source tree contains an unexpanded variable:" \
              "$src — this is the v0.6.4b2 defect" >&2
         exit 1 ;;
esac

if [ -d "$src/.git" ]; then
  echo "platterpus: reusing existing clone, fetching $branch"
  git -C "$src" remote set-url origin "$url"
  git -C "$src" fetch --force origin "$branch"
else
  echo "platterpus: no clone at $src — cloning $branch"
  git clone --branch "$branch" "$url" "$src"
fi
# Detach onto the verified commit — the FULL one when we have it, because a short
# name is resolved as a ref before it is resolved as a commit, so a tag or branch
# spelled like the pin would win. `--force` discards a half-finished previous
# attempt; the tree is a build cache we own, never the user's work.
git -C "$src" checkout --force --detach "${full:-$pin}"

# fork's meson `vcs_tag` prints `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, and git sizes a
# short hash by how many objects the repository holds: seven characters until
# a clone passes about 16,000 objects, eight after. The fork's repository passed
# that line with `.29`, so a reused clone built a tag ending `-g8d2ca726` where
# the published build, and the pin, end `-g8d2ca72`, and the check
# below refused a correct build (the owner's install of 0.7.120, 2026-11-04).
# Seven, git's own floor, is what the fork publishes; git still lengthens a

# are irreversible. Verifying only after them means a failed check reports the
# problem accurately and still leaves the wrong ripper on the ripping path,

# point of no return.

      *"($5"[0-9a-f]*)

             "differently, so the binary's tag would not match the pin" >&2 ;;

src="$HOME/$1"
url="$2"
branch="$3"
pin="$4"

# (the one place in this script that wants splitting), because it is either

echo "platterpus: cwd=$(pwd)"
echo "platterpus: source tree=$src"
echo "platterpus: requested pin=$pin branch=$branch"

  /*) : ;;

     exit 1 ;;
esac
case "$src" in
  *'$'*) echo "platterpus: FATAL source tree contains an unexpanded variable:" \
              "$src — this is the v0.6.4b2 defect" >&2

  git -C "$src" remote set-url origin "$url"
  git -C "$src" fetch --force origin "$branch"
else

  git clone --branch "$branch" "$url" "$src"

# name is resolved as a ref before it is resolved as a commit, so a tag or branch

      *"($5"[0-9a-f]*)

    exit 1 ;;
